summary: Analysis of pretreatment candidates identifies a high density of dual-role features. Radiographic features (288, 290, 294) and serum markers (295, 296, 297) consistently act as both confounders and effect modifiers. Molecular markers (289, 291) show strong evidence for effect modification but lack sufficient outcome signal to be classified as confounders, likely acting as instruments for treatment selection. Evidence for ROS1 rearrangement (292) and RSV status (293) was insufficient to establish a causal role.
